question: In which of the following years did Mahatma Gandhi lead the Dandi March?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1930**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the Salt March, was led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930.
 
• It was a 24-day, 240-mile (390 km) march from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi.
 
• The march was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly.
 
• Gandhi and his followers produced salt from the seawater in defiance of British law, which prohibited Indians from collecting or selling salt independently.
 
• The Dandi March was a significant event in the Indian independence movement and garnered worldwide attention and support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyagraha**

 
 
• It is a form of nonviolent resistance or civil resistance initiated by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The Dandi March was a part of the broader Satyagraha movement.
 
 
 
• **Salt Acts**
 
 
• The British Salt Acts prohibited Indians from collecting or selling salt, a staple in their diet.
 
• The Dandi March directly challenged these acts, making the production of salt a form of civil disobedience.
 
 
 
• **Impact**
 
 
• The march inspired millions of Indians to join the cause for independence.
 
• It drew significant international attention to the Indian independence movement.
